source.title: Mapping the Solution-Set Structure of Grokking on Latin Squares
source.authors: Zi-Han Gu; Lu-Lu Zhao; Tian-Yi Ma; Hua Zhang; Wen-Bo Su; Ya-Nan Cao; Yue Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a different model on modular addition and related Latin-square tasks and reports training-to-test transitions, rather than reproducing the original model and setup. Its minimum-norm endpoint theory does not measure training delay.
record.gate_note: The q=97 relabelled-addition runs directly report memorization followed by generalization. The paper explicitly says these runs do not certify membership in the minimum-norm endpoint set. The q=64 runs report finite-training transitions and final accuracies, not endpoint phases. The coverage thresholds in Table 3 do not measure how delay changes as training-set size shrinks. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The main contribution is theory about minimum-norm endpoint sets, which has no time index. The finite-training experiments, though, report memorise-then-generalise curves on new algorithmic settings: relabelled addition at q=97 and other group tables at q=64. These use a pair-embedding one-hidden-layer ReLU network trained with SGD and weight decay. That bears on V1 in a new setting (T3), rather than being a different method aimed at the original delay question (T2).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors' headline is theoretical: every finite abelian group family is asymptotically all-good (every minimum-norm endpoint generalises), while uniform random Latin squares defeat any observation-based learner. Relabelling preserves endpoint generalisation despite dense polynomial forms, and composite-order experiments suggest coarse factors are recovered before exact labels. They stress that the endpoint theory says nothing about training timescales.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests modular addition and delayed generalization with a pair-embedding one-hidden-layer ReLU network and also uses relabelled and Latin-table tasks. The reported training runs use a different model/protocol from a direct reproduction; the endpoint theory is a separate object from training dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: For relabelled addition, transition timing varies with optimization seed: the paper attributes about 93% of transition-midpoint variance to that seed. The q=64 coverage experiment uses nested, label-stratified masks; it does not measure delay as coverage changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Asymptotically, the worst minimum-norm endpoint for abelian group tables generalises at any fixed observation fraction. Under a uniform random Latin square, no observation-based learner succeeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether minimum-norm endpoints generalise is set by task structure: abelian group tables are all-good, while uniform Latin squares are unlearnable.

fits_no_version.finding: For C2^3×R8, binary-factor accuracy is 0.948 at 20% coverage while exact accuracy is 0.0169. Exact accuracy rises at higher nested coverages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On composite-order tasks, coarse output factors are recovered before exact labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the relabelled-addition orbit, about 93% of transition-midpoint variance comes from the optimisation seed; the task-seed effect is not significant (p≈0.33).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking delay varies mainly with optimisation randomness, while the final outcome is stable within a task orbit.

record.problems: The empirical q=97 comparison uses 30 relabelled-addition runs and 24 completed Latin controls; two planned control seeds were not completed. q=64 results use six runs per family and label-stratified masks, unlike the theoretical uniform-mask law. Finite-training runs do not certify minimum-norm endpoints. The study does not test the claim that delay increases as training data shrink.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports minimum coverage thresholds for exact accuracy after a fixed training horizon, not delay as a function of training-set size, so it is not recorded as a V1 result. Other factor-quotient resolutions and intervention audits in Sections D.4–D.5 concern the distinct coarse-factor construct and are not catalogued as tests of the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. Table 3 gives only coverage thresholds, not delays.
Gradual circuit formation, removal of memorising components, and progress measures anticipating the jump. A Fourier carrier is constructed in theory, but it is not measured in training.
Non-algorithmic data and initialisation-scale or lazy-to-rich switches.
Weight decay selecting an efficient circuit, critical dataset size, and ungrokking. The endpoint theory assumes a minimum-norm objective but does not test these predictions.
Identity of the algorithms learned across runs.
Optimizer and floating-point artifact controls. Runs are float64 with SGD, but there is no comparison against alternatives.

missing.what: Bank of nine named polynomial rules, 81 runs: six families transition in all nine repeats, three cross-term variants show none. This bears on whether V1 holds across algorithmic rules.
Product ladder C64→C8×R8→C4×R16→C2×R32→R64, showing gradual loss of exact completion as the random residual grows; also the exact accuracies in Table 6.
Sparse perturbations of the cyclic table give a crossover at about 2–5% corruption (40 runs).
Sixteen Transformer runs under the same protocol never reach sustained memorisation, so no grokking is observed. These are not comparable endpoints.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. Only V1 has verdicts. Chance-level plateau values are not given numerically; the transition criterion is plateau-relative (Appendix D.1). Figure 2's axis is labelled 'Epoch' in one place but the text uses updates. The q=64 runs use label-stratified masks and fixed width 512, unlike the theory's setup. The minimum-norm theory is consistent in spirit with V5's low-norm account, but it tests neither a critical dataset size nor ungrokking.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether the optimization delay grows as the training set shrinks.
It does not test gradual formation of a Fourier generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or whether continuous progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule setting, or initialization-scale/weight-norm lazy-to-rich intervention is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning setting is tested.
The endpoint theory uses a minimum-norm objective, but the study does not test whether weight decay selects a more efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
Relabelled tasks are compared by generalization outcomes, but the study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts as causes of the delay.

relation.reason: The study reports its own memorization-to-generalization trajectories and held-out endpoints, alongside theory about idealized minimum-norm endpoint sets.

tranche.reason: Finite-training experiments report delayed generalization in relabelled addition and additional group-table and partly structured Latin-table settings.

source_check.notes: The q=64 nominal 30% masks contain 1216/4096 cells (29.6875%); the q=97 split contains 2823/9409 cells. Relative transitions permit imperfect endpoints, and finite-training predictors do not certify the theoretical minimum-norm endpoint set or test whether smaller datasets increase delay.
